steps: Uncrate & fit the base

Remove the crate top, supports and plastic cover (leg units: loosen the nuts holding the supports). Fit the legs with the unit on its back; the stove must be installed with its pedestal or leg kit attached.

1. Remove the crate top and supports, then the plastic cover.
  2. Leg units: loosen the nuts holding the supports to the unit and remove the stove from them.
  3. Leg model: with the unit on its back, insert each leg around the first nut, between the leg adapter flange and the washer and second nut.
  4. Align the guides cast into the leg tops with the notches in the ash box mounting flanges, then tighten the bolts.
The rating label requires the appliance to be installed with the pedestal or leg kit attached.
Optional ash cleanout

Remove the ash drawer front cover and the top-left knock-out, then fit the ash dump from under the firebox with its gasket, release handle forward and on the left. Snug the nuts to gently compress the gasket and install the ash pan.

1. Pedestal: remove the centre screw and lift the ash drawer front cover plate off its bottom tab. Leg: remove the two screws on either side of the leg ash box front cover.
  2. Remove the knock-out in the top left corner of the opening.
  3. Under the stove, remove the ash cleanout hole cover plate and gasket; discard the plate.
  4. Put the supplied gasket(s) around the upper tube of the ash dump mechanism and insert it from underneath, up into the hole and over the two bolts. The release handle faces forward, on the left.
  5. Re-attach the nuts on the carriage bolts and tighten to gently compress the gasket.
  6. Install the new ash pan in the pedestal or leg ash box.

The manual lists the ash cleanout as optional on the Vista LE. The firebrick floor layout changes when an ash dump is fitted.
Floor protector

On a combustible floor use continuous non-combustible ember protection. USA: 16" front and 8" to the sides of the door opening, min. 33 3/8" × 35", and under the connector plus 2" each side; Canada: 18" firing side and 8" other sides, min. 40 3/4" × 45".
Position for clearances
Place the stove and protector to the clearance chart: 10" side, 10" back, 7" corner with a single-wall connector; 8", 8", 5" with double-wall. Combustible alcove: 7' min. height, 3' max. depth.
Chimney & connector

Listed UL-103 HT (USA) or ULC-S629 (Canada) chimney, or a lined masonry chimney for solid fuel, with a 6 inch flue and 15 feet minimum system height. Exit 3 feet above the roof and two feet above the highest projection within 10 feet; dedicated flue, no air distribution duct, not in a fireplace.

Flue sizeSame as stove outlet (6 inches)
Min. system height15 feet from base of appliance
Double-wall connectorUL-103 HT (USA) · ULC S-641 (Canada)
Single-wall connector6" diameter, 24 gauge black, clean and new

Single-wall pipe: as short and straight as possible, crimped (male) ends pointing down, secured at every joint and the collar with 3 sheet metal screws. It must not pass through an attic, roof space, closet or similar concealed space, floor or ceiling; through a combustible wall, follow CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211. With a listed chimney and double-wall connector, install per that manufacturer's requirements.
Run the chimney & connector

Plumb-bob from the flue centre to mark the ceiling and roof, check joists and rafters, then install the listed chimney to the rain cap. Slip the crimped end of the pipe inside the stove collar, fix with three screws, and build up to the chimney using the approved adapter.

1. Position the floor protection and stove per the clearance diagram.
  2. Hang a plumb-bob over the exact centre of the flue pipe to mark the ceiling and roof holes.
  3. Check for floor joists, ceiling joists and rafters; adjust and reconfirm clearances to combustibles.
  4. Install the listed chimney from the ceiling to the rain cap per its manufacturer (this may include framing in holes).
  5. Slip the crimped edge of the pipe inside the stove collar and secure with three screws through the collar holes.
  6. Add the remaining lengths up to the chimney and join them with the manufacturer's approved adapter; a slip section helps.

Offsets: screw all listed connector, offset elbows and chimney sections together with at least three sheet metal screws per joint, and support with the chimney maker's listed offset support. Minimum ceiling height 7'. The venting figure (p. 20) warns the unit may be harder to start, and asks for as much vertical length as possible in the first section of pipe.

Through a combustible wall (NFPA 211)

System A · brick wall + fireclay liner12 in. to combustibles
System B · insulated listed chimney length9 in. to combustibles
System C · ventilated sheet steel thimble6 in. to combustibles
System D · insulated chimney pass-through2 in. to combustibles

Keep the vapour barrier intact wherever components penetrate to the exterior. Construction details for each system are on pp. 22–23.
Combustion air

Room air enters through the ash box enclosure; outside air uses the 4" Intake Starter and 4" i.d. metal flex, through the floor (ventilated crawl space or ducted outdoors) or the wall behind. Outside air is required in mobile homes and, in a residence, requires securing the stove to the structure.

Through the floor

  • Leg model: cut a hole behind the ash box enclosure big enough for 4" metal flex. With the stove in place, attach the 4" Intake Starter to the ash box enclosure and connect to the floor with 4"(100mm) i.d. metal flex pipe.
  • Pedestal model: cut a 4" (100mm) hole anywhere inside the pedestal perimeter, cover it with a 4" x 4" rodent screen, leave the cover over the hole on the back of the pedestal and set the stove over the hole.

From behind

Use a 4"(100mm) air intake through the wall behind the unit, the 4" Intake Starter on the rear of the ash box enclosure and metal flex between them. Pedestal model: move the rear cover plate to the hole under the pedestal first.

Consult the local building code or CAN/CSA-B365 first. Keep the room well ventilated: negative pressure can pull fumes into the living area.
Mobile home extras

Outside air kit and a listed double-wall connector with a ULC-S629 or UL-103HT chimney are required; no horizontal connector and never in a sleeping room. Lag the stove to the floor with two 1/4" x 2" or longer lag screws through the legs or pedestal base, and keep the floor, wall and roof structure intact.
Optional blower

The kit can be fitted any time, following its own instructions; route the three-prong cord away from the heater, never beneath it. Confirm the kit part number and amp rating, which differ between the label and p. 25.
Firebrick layout
Rear wall first ("A" bricks behind and under the brick rail tabs), then each side wall, then the floor, which differs with and without an ash dump. One brick is left over as a spare.

A8 7/8" x 4 3/8" x 1 1/4"
B8 7/8" x 2 1/8" x 1 1/4"
C5 3/4" x 4 3/8" x 1 1/4"
D4 3/8" x 3 1/4" x 1 1/4"
E7" x 3 1/4" x 1 1/4"
F4 1/4" x 2 1/8" x 1 1/4"
  1. Rear wall: stand an "A" brick behind the brick rail tab and slide it toward the centre; slide a second "A" under the tab; repeat for the other rear "A" bricks.
  2. Each side wall: stand two "A" bricks and a narrow "B", place a "D" on top tucked behind the brick rail, then slide an "E" under the rail tab, resting on the three below.
  3. Floor with ash dump: two "A" on the floor, a third "A" against the rear wall, and the "C" beside the ash dump against the left side wall. Without ash dump: four "A" pushed to the back.
  4. Front row: a short "F" at the right, a long "B" in the centre, the last "F" at the left. A gap remains behind the ash dump.

Replace broken or missing bricks; never elevate the fire on a grate or andirons.

light.title: Starting a fire
light.html:
Light the stove with newspaper and dry kindling. Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire.

  1. Move the air control to High, all the way to the left, and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the stove. Crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it, then add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, start normal burning.
Your first 2-3 fires bake the paint on. Keep the room well ventilated: open all windows and doors. The smoke and fumes can bother some people. Follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) sheet that came with your stove.
Build the fire right on the firebricks. Don't raise it on a grate or andirons.

burn.title: Air control, reloading & overnight burns
burn.html:
The air control sets how hot and how long the fire burns. It runs from "H" (high, all the way to the left) to "L" (low). The right setting depends on your wood, the weather and your chimney, so find it by trial and error and note it for next time.

  • Smoke pouring down across the glass (a "waterfall") means you turned the air down too soon or too low.
  • Use high only to start a fire or heat up a fresh load.

Adding wood

  1. Turn the air to high and let the fire brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff back into the room.
  3. Load logs endwise, up to 18" long, with space for air between them. Don't load so high that opening the door would be hazardous.
  4. For a clean burn, add two or three logs at a time and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes. After that you can turn it down a lot.

Overnight

Use unsplit logs, never green or wet wood. Char the load completely on high before turning the air down. To restart, rake the hot embers forward, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to high. Once the wood has charred, reset the air.

The minimum burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations.

wood.title: Choosing and testing your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood burns cleaner and gives more heat than softwood or green wood.

  • Season wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.
  • Logs can be up to 18" long; 16" is ideal.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and goes out often. It can cut the stove's output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. It's dry if it burns on more than one side within one minute. It's damp if it turns black and lights within three minutes. If it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes, it's too wet. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Treated or salt-water wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, cardboard, plywood or particleboard, plastics, rubber, yard waste, railroad ties, building debris, paints or solvents. Some release toxic fumes. Charcoal can make deadly carbon monoxide. Salt-water wood and garbage destroy metal and void the warranty.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when the stove is cold.

  • Never scrape it with anything that could scratch it, and don't use abrasive cleaners.
  • Don't slam the door. Make sure no logs stick out where they could hit the glass when you close it.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good burning with dry wood, and fairly clean pipes. A black, greasy film that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That deposit is building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the stove. Use only 10-1/2" x 16-1/2" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer. Don't substitute any other type.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the stove is cold. When ash is 3" to 4" deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" of ash on the floor of the firebox to help keep a hot charcoal bed.

Ash cleanout (optional on the Vista LE)

  1. The ash dump handle is under the ash lip, on the left. Pull it out 1/2" and turn it clockwise to unlock the dump.
  2. Hold the handle open and pull ashes into the opening. Avoid large embers, which still have heat value.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Make sure the ash dump door is properly closed, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the firebox floor.
  4. Lift out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container and put it back properly seated.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Disposing of ashes

Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a non-combustible floor or the ground, well away from anything that can burn. Keep it closed until all cinders have cooled, and put no other waste in it.

chimney.title: Creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar and vapours that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. When creosote catches fire, it burns extremely hot. Some is inevitable; regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

  • Have the chimney and connector pipe inspected at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Burn dry wood with plenty of air, and don't turn the air down too soon after loading.
  • Don't burn trash, cardboard or Christmas tree limbs.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get ready to leave. Follow your family's plan and meet at your spot outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Afterwards, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before your next fire. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.
A certified sweep or installer (NFI, CSIA, WETT or APC) is strongly recommended for chimney inspection and service.

overfire.title: Over-firing and draft
overfire.html:
Over-firing means trying to get more heat than the stove is designed for. It can permanently damage the stove and chimney, can be hazardous, and may void the warranty.

Signs of over-firing: a glowing red top, chimney connector or chimney.

How to avoid it

  • Use high only to start a fire or heat up a fresh load, not longer than it takes to char the wood.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning, and open it only to add wood. This stove isn't designed for open-door burning.
  • Keep the ash dump closed while the fire burns.

Draft

Draft is the pull that moves air through the stove and up the chimney. It depends on the chimney's length, local geography, nearby obstructions and other factors.

  • Too much draft can overheat the stove. An uncontrollable burn or a glowing red stove part or chimney are the signs.
  • Too little draft can puff smoke back into the room and plug the chimney. Smoke leaking from the stove or connector joints is the sign.

care.title: Gaskets and regular checks
care.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping. Use only parts supplied by the manufacturer for maintenance and replacements.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracks) · door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rails and tabs · air riser tube · back of the airwash chamber · baffle locking pin · boost tube cover · baffle tubes
At chimney cleaningTop baffle board and blanket · baffle · top heat shield and bolt · baffle gasket · brick rails · manifold

Door gasket

The door seals with 3/4" fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure. Inspect it now and then, and replace it when needed with gasket kit 80000670 from your dealer.

  • Some baffle warping, up to 1/4", is normal. Replace the baffle if it's warped more, cracked or broken.
  • Keep the front of the firebox, where boost air enters, clear of built-up ash.
  • Clean a plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
Never run the stove with the baffle, tubes or insulation removed. If you find damage, call your dealer. Running with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

blower.title: Using the optional blower
blower.html:
The optional blower kit can be added at any time. It has a three-prong power cord: keep the cord away from the stove and never run it underneath.

Match it to the air setting

  • Air control on "L" (low): run the blower on Low.
  • Air control between "L" and "H": pick any blower speed you like.

Auto or manual

Auto: set the rocker switch on the side of the fan housing to "Auto" and choose a speed. The fan comes on as the stove heats up, and shuts off after the fire is out and the stove has cooled.

Manual: set the rocker switch to "Man" and choose a speed. This bypasses the temperature sensor, so the blower won't shut off until you turn it off. You can switch modes or change speed any time.

Vacuum the grill openings on the back and bottom of the blower casing at least every six months to clear dust and debris.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Contact can burn skin.
  • Hot glass will cause burns. Never let children touch it.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away from the stove.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning.
  • Don't store wood inside the stove's clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal. Keep the area free of furniture, newspapers and other loose combustibles.
  • Never alter the air control. Tampering voids the warranty and can be very hazardous.
  • Teach everyone at home how to run the stove safely, especially what to do in a chimney fire.

Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors

Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended in the area where the stove is installed. Smoke alarms may go off more often at first, from curing paint or from leaving the door open by accident. Don't disconnect them.

conflicts.issue: Connector clearances: the rating label gives Vista LE side wall / back wall / corner to connector of 19-1/2" / 14-3/8" / 16-1/2" (single wall) and 17-1/2" / 12-3/8" / 14-1/2" (double wall). The Figure 13 clearance drawing on p. 17 shows 19 7/8", 17 3/8", 22 7/8" (single wall) and 17 7/8", 15 3/8", 20 7/8" (double wall), with no text saying what each measures (its 17 7/8" is also paired with 505mm). Unit clearances (10/10/7 and 8/8/5) agree.

US floor protector side extension: p. 16 says 8" to the sides of the fuel loading door opening (Figure 11 shows 8"); the rating label's US values are G 16", H 5" (side), I 0" (back). The reference point for H isn't stated in text.
Blower kit part number: the rating label says fan kit part # 11140001; p. 25 says optional blower kit Part #: WODC.BLOWB.
Blower electrical rating: the rating label says 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP; p. 25 says 115 volts AC-1.02 amps.

review.notes: Both models share one manual, one rating label and one set of figures (output/efficiency table, clearances, floor protection, venting), so no spec card needed separate per-model numbers. In the text, the models differ only in: the p. 13 dimension drawings (Vista LE pedestal, Vista LE leg, Vista Classic LE), the ash cleanout (stated as optional on the Vista LE, p. 8), and the parts lists (Classic enamel parts p. 30, Vista LE p. 31). These are summarised on the Versions card. The p. 13 drawings give different values per version (e.g. 24 7/8" and 28" on the Classic where the Vista LE shows 25 3/4" and 27 1/4"), but the text doesn't say which dimension each is, so none were transcribed. The leg drawing also pairs 25 3/4" with 635mm where the pedestal drawing pairs it with 660mm. The rating label clearance blocks are headed VISTA LE (plus ALDERLEA T4 LE, a model not in this guide). The label certifies both Vista models but lists no separate Classic values; treated as covering the Vista family, which the manual's figure titles also call VISTA LE. The p. 3 output/efficiency table is scrambled in the layout text. The label-value pairing (LHV 78%, HHV 72%, EPA output 13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr, maximum 18 inches, ideal 16 inches, fuel seasoned cord wood) was confirmed from the raw text extraction of the same page. Output range: table 13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr; the paragraph on p. 3 rounds it to 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr. Both are shown; not treated as a conflict. The catalog's btu_output_epa 23200 matches the rounded figure. The rating label states an 18" minimum between a single-wall connector and combustibles (reducible with listed shields), while its as-tested single-wall connector clearances are 14-3/8" to 19-1/2", marked as tested with a pipe shield possibly required by local authorities. Both are shown as a warning in specClear. The venting figures (pp. 20-21) are diagrams. Only clearly labelled callouts were used (48" combustibles in front of the unit, 7' minimum ceiling height). Others (56-3/4" minimum, 12" first pipe section) were not transcribed. The manual has stale cross-references: p. 19 'see Figure #3, Page 7'; p. 24 says outside air 'See page 18' (Combustion Air is on p. 19); p. 29 says 'see page 11' for draft (p. 11 is baffle removal). The firebrick layout figure on p. 25 is captioned 'Neo 1.6 LE'; the p. 31 parts list shows the firebrick set as 'NEO 1.6 LE / Vista LE'.
